_readme: Reading paths for /start/. Every id must be a file in src/content/figures; the build fails otherwise. Keep each 'why' to one plain line.

firstRead.why: The clearest case of a teaching built on one question, Who am I?, and one of the best-connected names on the tree.
The Chicago speech of 1893 and Advaita turned into a creed of service.
A Sanskrit scholar in a Mysore palace who joined posture to breath and trained the teachers of the world's yoga classes.
Truth and nonviolence treated as a spiritual practice, with every vow and fast described as an experiment.
A reading of the Buddha as a guide for this world, and a direct challenge to caste.

paths.title: Meditation and self-inquiry
paths.blurb: Teachers who pointed attention back at the one who is looking.

steps.why: The source of modern self-inquiry and the question the others keep returning to.
A devotee of Krishna who met Ramana and later carried the teaching to Western seekers in Lucknow.
The teacher who turned his lineage from slow meditation to direct understanding.
Siddharameshwar's student, who kept one instruction and taught it from a Bombay loft.
A police officer in Kerala who taught the Self by careful reasoning.
A Buddhist route to the same territory, through insight meditation learned in Burma.

paths.title: Yoga as practised today
paths.blurb: How postures and breathing became a worldwide daily practice.

steps.why: Hatha yoga taken into a laboratory and a scientific journal.
Posture joined to breath, and the teacher of the teachers.
Precision, props and the manual that put postures in homes worldwide.
Linked postures turned into Ashtanga Vinyasa, the most influential vigorous yoga of the late twentieth century.
A doctor turned monk at Rishikesh, whose disciples carried his yoga round the world.
Sivananda's student, who built the Bihar School of Yoga and taught yoga nidra.

paths.title: Devotion and grace
paths.blurb: Paths in which love of God and chanting the Name carry the whole weight.

steps.why: A magistrate who wrote Chaitanya's theology for a modern, English-reading public.
His son, who founded the Gaudiya Math and sent its first missionaries abroad.
The Gaudiya monk who sailed to America at sixty-nine and planted Krishna devotion in more than a hundred cities.
An engineer who left home in 1922 with one mantra and taught that Ram is everything.
A Hanuman devotee who wrote nothing and taught by feeding people.
Love expressed as an embrace and as service.

paths.title: Social reform and caste
paths.blurb: Teachers for whom the spiritual question and the question of caste were the same question.

steps.why: A Nadar teacher of southern Travancore whose message was that the lowly must be raised.
A Poona reformer who read the Puranas as the record of a conquest.
The argument that sacred learning belongs to everyone.
Advaita in Malayalam verse, with a social programme drawn out of it.
The rationalist answer, which asked Tamils to give up god, scripture and priest.
Twenty-one years of choosing a religion, ending in a Buddhism for this world.

paths.title: Science and reason
paths.blurb: Teachers who tested scripture by reason, or put the practices on a laboratory bench.

steps.why: Reason as the test of every scripture, and the start of the book's story.
The claim that the Vedas, read correctly, agree with reason in every line.
Yoga measured with instruments and reported in a journal.
A monk who let American scientists wire him to their instruments.
A meditation course that staked its reputation on laboratory science.
Kundalini described in plain detail and proposed as a biological engine of evolution.

paths.title: Women teachers
paths.blurb: Women who became gurus and led movements of their own.

steps.why: Ramakrishna's wife, who became guru and mother to the order his disciples built.
A village girl who initiated herself and taught for sixty years that one reality wears every form.
A widowed mother who taught meditation from a small flat and trained founders of American insight meditation.
A teacher who said she could awaken kundalini in a whole hall at once.
A fisherman's daughter who made the embrace into a form of darshan.
A founder who handed his fortune and his movement to a committee of young women.

paths.title: The Western reach
paths.blurb: How Indian teachings crossed the oceans, by lecture hall, book, mail course and ashram.

steps.why: Chicago in 1893, where the crossing began in earnest.
A Buddhist who spoke at the same Chicago parliament.
A court musician who took the Chishti Sufi path to Europe and America.
Kriya Yoga for America by lecture, by mail and through one famous book.
A trunk of translations and a temple movement built from New York outward.
Meditation as a fixed course, taught to millions.
The guru's awakening touch given as a public initiation in India and the West.

paths.title: The lineages that cross
paths.blurb: Chains of teachers that run across religions, and the people standing where they meet.

steps.why: A fakir in a mosque, worshipped in his lifetime by Hindus and Muslims alike.
A doctor who spent a year at Shirdi and then taught the young Meher Baba.
A Zoroastrian from Pune who named five living saints, Hindu and Muslim, as his masters.
The claim to be Sai Baba of Shirdi reborn, and a movement built on the unity of religions.
A Jain jeweller and poet to whom Gandhi wrote when his faith was in doubt.
Where Jain, Vaishnava and Christian threads meet in one practice of truth.
A Kerala-born Muslim who, by his own account, trained with a Natha yogi and teaches Kriya Yoga.
